name: WISPFI
full_name: WISP Searches on a Fiber Interferometer
summary: A hollow-core photonic-crystal-fiber interferometer in a magnetic field, testing axion–photon mixing through photon disappearance.
detection_principle: A hollow-core fiber in one arm is placed in a magnetic field; a phase-locked, modulated Mach–Zehnder interferometer reads out amplitude differences from resonant conversion.

status.label: Prototype experiments / R&D
status.evidence: 2025 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

collaboration.name: WISPFI Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Prototype
key_parameters.value: 2 W, 1550 nm laser; 1 m fiber; approximately 2 T magnetic field

results.summary: The 2025 paper reports the first prototype and projected sensitivity, not yet a dark-matter-exclusion result.

science_scope: Produces and detects axions or dark-sector particles in the laboratory, rather than directly measuring Galactic-halo dark-matter flux. It tests interactions of dark-matter candidates; identifying a discovered particle as dark matter would also require establishing its cosmic abundance.
